title: LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury in Mice
author: Laura Ruiz Remolina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j8ecrte

steps.title: Isolate the Trachea
steps.instruction: Isolate the trachea, ensuring the conjunctiva and surrounding fat are cleaned thoroughly.

steps.title: Secure the Trachea
steps.instruction: Secure the trachea using a thread and needle to prevent leakage during lavage.

substeps.instruction: Pass a thread under the trachea using tweezers without squeezing.
Make a small cut in the trachea with scissors and insert the tip of a round-tip needle.
Tighten the knot to secure the needle, then tie a second tightening knot.

steps.title: Perform Bronchoalveolar Lavage
steps.instruction: Perform bronchoalveolar lavage by introducing heparinized PBS into the lungs and recovering the wash.

substeps.instruction: Gradually introduce 500ul of 1X heparinized PBS into the lungs until the chest swells.
Slowly recover the washing fluid, tilting the mouse body slightly if necessary.
Note that recovery of 300-400ul is normal due to needle dead volume.

steps.title: Collect and Process Lungs
steps.instruction: Collect the lungs and divide them for fixation and freezing.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the collected lungs in saline.
Cut a portion of the lung and place it in a Falcon tube with 10% formaldehyde for fixation, using gauze to ensure the fabric is well embedded.
Store the remaining tissue in packets, flash-freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Analyze Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Process the sample for cell counting.

substeps.instruction: Count the cells using a Neubauer chamber.
